D010-D006_h001.question:
"It's been a rough year, doctor. I feel like I'm on a rollercoaster I can't get off. For about two months, I was just...on fire. My mind was racing, I couldn't stop talking, often interrupting people because the words just *had* to come out. I had so much energy I'd barely sleep, just buzzing, wanting to do everything at once. I even sank a significant chunk of my savings into some really questionable online ventures, convinced they were brilliant ideas. My interest in sex went through the roof, which was quite out of character. During that time, I also started seeing things – fleeting shadows, sometimes even distinct figures in my peripheral vision that weren't really there. And I became absolutely convinced my boyfriend was cheating on me, despite him swearing up and down he wasn't.

But then, it crashed. For the past five months, it’s been the complete opposite. A heavy, constant sadness has settled over me. I can’t feel joy anymore; everything I used to love just feels flat and meaningless. Even picking out what to wear in the morning feels like an impossible task. It’s draining, and I can barely function most days. The strange thing is, the visions and the belief about my boyfriend, they disappeared once the high energy left. They only ever happened when I was feeling that intense, wired way."
D010-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h001.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h002.question:
For the past two months, I’ve been feeling an endless surge of energy. I barely sleep, and my mind races with ideas. I’ve been so irritable, snapping at my husband over the smallest things, which isn't like me at all. I found myself talking non-stop during my census rounds; I just couldn’t seem to keep quiet. I even started calling old acquaintances I haven't spoken to in years, just to chat. I ended up putting a good chunk of our savings into a "guaranteed" investment opportunity I saw online, a sure thing, even though my husband warned against it.

Around the same time all this started, I’ve also been experiencing some really strange things. I keep tasting this awful metallic flavor, like pennies, even after brushing my teeth. And I’m absolutely convinced that my insides are rotting away, that my organs are dissolving, despite what the doctor says. These peculiar thoughts and tastes only started when I got this burst of energy and talked more than usual.

Now, though, that burst has faded. For about five months before this, I was in a terrible slump. It was like a thick fog in my head, making it hard to concentrate on anything, even simple tasks for the census. I just wanted to be left alone, and I pulled away from everyone, even my closest friends. I felt constantly sad and hopeless.
D010-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h002.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h003.question: "It’s been a crazy few months, doc. Like, for about two months, I was on top of the world. I barely slept, just coded for hours, sometimes days, without stopping. D010-D006_h004.question: It's been about seven months now. For the first two, I was on top of the world, barely sleeping. D010-D006_h005.question:
Lately, things have been an absolute rollercoaster, and I honestly don't know what's going on. For about two months, I was on top of the world. I barely slept but felt incredibly alive, like I could conquer my entire Ph.D. in a week. I’d just talk and talk, bouncing from one idea to the next, almost like I couldn’t get the words out fast enough. My professors probably thought I was brilliant, but my friends said I was being too much. It wasn't just my studies, either; I found myself being really impulsive, especially with dating. I was sleeping with people I barely knew and doing things I'd never normally consider. The oddest thing, though, was I started getting these weird tastes in my mouth, metallic or sometimes impossibly sweet, even when I wasn't eating anything. And I felt like everyone on campus was talking about me, not in a bad way, but like they were all part of some bigger plan just for me. It was all very intense, and it definitely messed up my ability to focus on my research.

But that all crashed a few months ago, and for the past five months, I've just felt… empty. It's like the vibrant colors drained out of everything. Nothing interests me anymore, not even the research I used to love. I just sit there, staring at my computer, and then scold myself for forgetting why I even opened it. The good news, if you can call it that, is that those strange tastes and the feeling of everyone watching me? They vanished as soon as that high feeling did. It's like they only show up when I'm feeling completely over the moon.
D010-D006_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h005.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h007.question:

One minute I'm soaring, like I could build a ship all on my own, the next I'm snapping at her for the smallest thing. I can't seem to stop moving; my hands always have to be doing something, fiddling, pacing. And my mouth… it just goes. I feel this intense pressure to talk, like if I stop, my thoughts will explode. It’s been during this time that things have gotten really strange. Sometimes I feel like bugs are crawling under my skin, tickling and squirming, even when there’s nothing there. And I keep seeing signs – I know it sounds crazy – that the whole world is about to fall apart. Like the very plates of the earth are shifting, and everything we know is going to collapse. It’s hard to focus on work when I’m convinced the sky is about to fall. These sensations and beliefs, they only surface when I’m feeling this heightened state of mind. They vanish when things calm down.

D010-D006_h008.question:

And at night, it's the worst – I keep feeling things crawling on my skin, like bugs or spiders, but when I look, there’s nothing there. It’s so unsettling. The strange thing is, all these weird thoughts and sensations, they only happen when I'm feeling this way, when I'm all revved up and irritable. Once these intense periods pass, those specific worries about my husband and the crawling feeling on my skin, they just disappear. It’s making it hard to manage my businesses, and my marriage is really suffering.

A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h023.question: "Lately, it's been a real rollercoaster, doc. For about two weeks, I was on top of the world. Just an incredible high, full of energy, like I could finally take on anything. My ex-wife, bless her heart, I was convinced she was still madly in love with me, sending me secret signals. I even heard her voice sometimes, whispering my name when no one was there… it felt so real. I just couldn't sit still or focus on one thing, my mind buzzing with a million ideas. But that all crashed down eventually. For the last two months, I've had zero get-up-and-go. Even getting out of bed feels like a monumental task. Everything is slow, my movements are sluggish, and honestly, sometimes I just wish I could disappear. The scary voices and the feeling she loved me, though, they only happen when I'm feeling that intense high, never when I’m down like this. It’s draining me, and it’s been impossible to do my rounds."

D010-D006_h024.question: Lately, things have been a blur, doctor. For the past two weeks, my brain has been racing. One minute I'm on top of the world, feeling invincible, the next I'm snapping at anyone who looks at me wrong. At work, it’s a nightmare. I can't sit still, constantly pacing the control room, and I've started so many new protocols I haven't finished a single one. It’s like my thoughts are on fast forward, and it's getting harder to keep track of the planes. And the voices... I hear them, quiet at first, then louder, whispering about how I'm being watched, that someone’s out to sabotage my career. Then there's the other side, the two months before all this started, when I couldn't care less about anything. My usual weekend hikes, even my favorite video games, felt pointless. I’d just pace my apartment, feeling this agonizing restlessness but no desire to do anything. Even then, when I had those sudden urges to just run into oncoming traffic, or jump from the tower, those whispers about being watched, they were gone. They only come around when I'm feeling this wired.

D010-D006_h025.question:
My name is Sarah, I'm 24 and a grad student. It’s hard to even know where to begin. For the past two weeks, it felt like I was on top of the world. My ideas were flowing, and I was working on so many different theories for my thesis, often all at once. I’d jump from one complex problem to another, convinced I was on the verge of a breakthrough in all of them. I felt totally euphoric, like I could conquer anything, and sleep became an unnecessary luxury. During this time, I started to notice some really strange things, too. I'd taste bitter almonds when nothing was there, or I’d be convinced that my classmates' casual conversations had hidden messages specifically about me, like they were sending me coded instructions through their regular chatter. I couldn't focus on just one thing, and life felt so utterly brilliant.

But then, before that, for about two months, it was the complete opposite. I moved so slowly, barely having the energy to get out of bed. My limbs felt heavy and dragging. All the success I’d had before, even getting into grad school, just didn’t matter. It was all meaningless. I kept thinking about how much I just wanted to disappear, wishing I wouldn’t wake up most mornings. It made it impossible to keep up with my studies or anything, really. The taste of almonds and the strange messages only started when I was feeling really high and energetic; they completely disappeared once I crashed.
D010-D006_h025.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D010-D006_h025.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
